title: Exodus 24 — The covenant ratification + the elders see the Elohim of Yisra'el on Sinai

translation.sourceText: Hebrew Masoretic text (Westminster Leningrad Codex base, Public Domain) — Tanach with Ta'amei Hamikra

citations: Gruber, Aspects of Nonverbal Communication in the Ancient Near East (Studia Pohl 12, 1980)
verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed wəʾel-mōšeh ʾāmar (fronted object) and wəhištaḥăwîtem mērāḥōq (Hishtaphel 2mp perfect consecutive). 'Bow down' (ASV 'worship') names the bodily act. It matches exodus-woh 20:5, which is signed off, and it leaves the context to show that this is worship.

wəniggaš mōšeh ləḇaddô ... wəhēm lōʾ yiggāšû wəhāʿām lōʾ yaʿălû ʿimmô: the graded access is rendered exactly, and the speech closes here. The reception note matches TBWTT ch. 3, which quotes the verse after Ex 19:23-24. It correctly says that the canon's 'the elders of Israel' paraphrases wəhēm. The line encodes no reading.
kol-diḇrê YHWH wəʾēṯ kol-hammišpāṭîm ... qôl ʾeḥāḏ ... naʿăśeh: exact; 'ordinances' (ASV) for mišpāṭîm is the corpus term.
wayyiḵtōḇ ... wayyaškēm babbōqer ... taḥaṯ hāhār ... šətêm ʿeśrēh maṣṣēḇâ: exact. 'At the foot of the mountain' gives the sense of taḥaṯ hāhār. The central maṣṣēḇâ and twelve-tribes entries apply.

wayyaʿălû ʿōlōṯ wayyizbəḥû zəḇāḥîm šəlāmîm laYHWH pārîm: zəḇāḥîm šəlāmîm is appositional, and 'of bulls' renders the clause-final pārîm (ASV 'of oxen'). The line follows the central olah and qorbanot renderings.
zāraq ʿal-hammizbēaḥ: 'dashed against' for zāraq, as distinct from hizzâ 'sprinkle'. This is the standard modern distinction (ASV 'sprinkled').
naʿăśeh wənišmāʿ: after 'we will do', šāmaʿ has the sense 'obey', as in the ASV, NRSV and NJPS. The literal 'hear' and b. Shabbat 88a are in the commentary.
wayyizrōq ʿal-hāʿām: same verb and rite as v 6, so 'dashed it on' is consistent. kāraṯ bərîṯ 'cut' follows the central entry.

citations: TBWTT ch. 3 (FR and EN, checked in torah-canon-citations.md)
verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed kəmaʿăśēh liḇnaṯ hassappîr ûḵəʿeṣem haššāmayim lāṭōhar. There is no ʾeḇen, so dropping the ASV's supplied 'stone' is correct, and 'the very skies' (physical sky) follows the ratified register rule. The English line is approved. Commentary fix: the reception note says the canon's English 'follows the ASV, including the supplied stone', but the canon's English ('a paved work of a sapphire stone, and as it were the body of heaven in his clearness') is the KJV wording, not the ASV. The French canon ('un ouvrage en plaque de saphir') has no 'pierre' and agrees with the line. Correct the note to say so. The same KJV/ASV slip should be fixed at 25:3, Num 21:9 and in the central nechoshet rationale. [Resolved at human sign-off, 2026-11-01: the requested fix was applied by the editor.]
wayyeḥĕzû ʾeṯ-hāʾĕlōhîm: the ḥāzâ/rāʾâ contrast is kept with 'beheld' (ASV), and ʾăṣîlê 'nobles' is the ASV word. The MT is translated over the LXX paraphrase.

wəhattôrâ wəhammiṣwâ ʾăšer kāṯaḇtî ləhôrōṯām: 'the law and the commandment' is the ASV and NRSV rendering, and the written object supports 'law'. NJPS has 'the teachings', and the yrh wordplay (ləhôrōṯām) keeps 'instruction' a live alternative. The note records the root but not NJPS; adding NJPS is recommended and does not block approval. The ambiguity of the explicative wə is preserved.
wîhôšuaʿ məšārəṯô ... har hāʾĕlōhîm: 'attendant' for məšārēṯ is accurate (NJPS). 'The mountain of the Elohim' follows the central har-sinai entry, as at 3:1.
šəḇû-lānû ḇāzeh ... mî-ḇaʿal dəḇārîm yiggaš ʾălēhem: 'whoever has a matter' is the correct sense of the idiom.
Exact. The articular heʿānān is rendered 'the cloud'.
wayyiškōn kəḇôḏ-YHWH 'dwelt' (central shakhan; ASV 'abode'); waykassēhû 'covered it' keeps the Hebrew's ambiguous object (mountain or Moses).

kəʾēš ʾōḵeleṯ rendered as a simile, with the English article added for the count noun. The reception note correctly reports TBWTT ch. 3 (craft, fire-like colour at departure); the canon quotation is KJV-worded ('the sight of the glory'). The line renders kāḇôḏ 'glory' and encodes no craft.

Forms are transliterated consistently (tz/q/ch/v/f rules), the ASV equivalence table is complete for the wave, and 'the Egyptians' for the population follows exodus-woh's published practice. claim_type direct is right for a presentation convention. Each listed site re-checked in the source. The source carries one Ketiv/Qere (Num 21:32) and one extraordinary point (Num 21:30, U+05C4 over the rēš of ʾăšer). The Deut 4:30 athnach is on hāʾēlleh, and Deut 4:37 has singular suffixes. Every MT reading is construable and the versions are recorded. The only error, the Ketiv vocalization at Num 21:32, is in that verse's commentary, not in this entry.

The clauses are sound and match the exodus-woh and Kings practice (checked: exodus-woh 20:3, 20 'elohim'; 1 Kgs 8:23 'no elohim like you'). One factual fix: the rationale argues that at Deut 4:7 the plural adjective qərōḇîm makes ʾĕlōhîm a class. Plural attributives also stand with ʾĕlōhîm of YHWH himself (Deut 5:26 ʾĕlōhîm ḥayyîm; Josh 24:19 ʾĕlōhîm qədōšîm; 1 Sam 17:26), so the adjective proves nothing. The comparison 'as YHWH our Elohim' carries the decision. Restate the argument on that basis, in all three overlays and in the DEU-WOH-4:7 commentary. [Resolved at human sign-off, 2026-11-01: the requested fix was applied by the editor.]

Correct. The Hebrew has no ʾeḇen, and the lapis-lazuli identification is standard. Fix one factual statement in the rationale: the canon's English of Ex 24:10 is the KJV wording ('the body of heaven in his clearness'), and the French canon ('plaque de saphir') has no 'stone' (see EXO-WOH-24:10).

founderDecisionRecommendations.F1-proper-names: Option (a) for this wave: keep the split, do not retro-edit signed-off chapters, and record it in the corpus. For the later normalization pass the reviewer recommends one form per name across the corpus. Prefer the transliterated 'Moshe'/'Par'oh', because they are the only English forms left in an otherwise transliterated Torah and the ASV equivalence table already serves readers of the canon's KJV-based English. Prefer the tz spelling 'Mitzrayim', since tz is already the Torah rule for every other tsade. Keep 'the Egyptians' for the population (amend the central gentilic 'Mitsri', which no volume uses), and bring isaiah-woh 'Egypt' into the same decision.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F2-torah: Retire the transliterated 'torah' at the next Exodus pass and apply the sense rule. Ex 13:9 'the law of YHWH' is a Deuteronomic-style formula (ASV, NRSV 'law'), and Ex 16:4 'my law' (ASV, NRSV) or 'my instruction' (NJPS 'teaching') is a founder preference. Keep Isaiah's 'teaching' as the prophetic clause of the same central entry.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F3-bara: Agree. Keep 'create' outside Gen 1 (Deut 4:32; Isaiah 40-65 already do), and add a scope sentence to central bara saying that 'shape' is the Gen 1 rendering only.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F4-teruma: Ratify 'oblation' with hērîm 'set apart'. It is lexically sound, already the corpus term in Ezekiel and Isa 40:20, and it removes the unsupported 'heave' etymology. Semver: minor is defensible because no shipped line changes, but renumber the three parallel 2.84.0 diffs sequentially.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F5-merism: Confirm 'the heavens and the earth' for the merism outside Gen 1 (exodus-woh 20:11; Deut 4:26, 39). State explicitly that the creation formulas of Isaiah ('created the skies', 'spread out the earth') render the physical sky 'skies', so that the two practices read as one rule.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F6-saraf: The Isaiah wave has already applied the same rule ('a fiery flying serpent' at Isa 14:29; 'seraphim' for the Isa 6 attendants). Promote one central śārāp̄ entry stating both clauses.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F7-herem: The Former Prophets decision is now visible ('devoted thing' / 'devote to destruction'). Adopt it at Num 21:2-3 (reviewer revise), promote a single central ḥērem entry, and reconcile isaiah-woh 43:28 'the ban'.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F8-deuteronomy-quotation: Confirm. It matches NJPS practice and the chapter applies it consistently (4:6, 10 inner double marks; 4:41 narration). Apply it unchanged to Deut 1-3 and 5.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F9-kapporet: Keep 'mercy-seat' (ASV, NRSV). It preserves the link with kippēr and Lev 16 that 'cover' loses, and the dispute is fully recorded in the commentary.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F10-next-exodus-pass: Agree with all three items (16:16 'souls'; the 'heavens' register check at 16:4; 17:14; 20:4, 11, 19; 13:9 and 16:4 'torah'). Add the FP1 shofar refId correction (EXO-WOH-20:15, not 20:18) to the merge checklist.

paragraphs.text: וְאֶל־מֹשֶׁ֨ה אָמַ֜ר עֲלֵ֣ה אֶל־יְהוָ֗ה אַתָּה֙ וְאַהֲרֹן֙ נָדָ֣ב וַאֲבִיה֔וּא וְשִׁבְעִ֖ים מִזִּקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֖ם מֵרָחֹֽק׃

i18n.en: And to Moses he said, "Come up to YHWH, you and Aharon, Nadav and Avihu, and seventy of the elders of Yisra'el, and bow down from afar.

notes.official:
*wəʾel-mōšeh ʾāmar* 'And to Moses he said': the speaker is YHWH, unnamed because the narrative resumes after the Book of the Covenant (20:19-23:33 MT); the fronted object marks a new instruction to Moses after the laws addressed to the people (Childs, *The Book of Exodus*, OTL, 1974; Propp, *Exodus 19-40*, AB 2A, 2006). *wəhištaḥăwîtem mērāḥōq* 'and bow down from afar' (draft and ASV 'worship'): the Hishtaphel of *ḥwh* is the act of prostration, and the line uses 'bow down', exodus-woh's rendering of the same verb at 20:5, under the Torah clause added to the central `hishtachavah-bow-down-obeisance-worship`. 'From afar' sets the first of the chapter's graded distances: the people below, the seventy elders part-way up (vv 9-11), Moses alone at the summit (vv 2, 12-18).

Nadav and Avihu (ASV Nadab and Abihu) are Aharon's elder sons (6:23; Lev 10:1-2); names follow `hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`, under which 'Moses' is the grandfathered exodus-woh English form.

paragraphs.text: וְנִגַּ֨שׁ מֹשֶׁ֤ה לְבַדּוֹ֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה וְהֵ֖ם לֹ֣א יִגָּ֑שׁוּ וְהָעָ֕ם לֹ֥א יַעֲל֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And Moses alone shall draw near to YHWH; but they shall not draw near, and the people shall not go up with him."

notes.official:
*wəniggaš mōšeh ləḇaddô ʾel-YHWH* 'And Moses alone shall draw near to YHWH'. *ngš* 'draw near' is the verb of approach to the holy (19:22; 20:18 MT = 20:21 ET), and the verse reserves it for Moses: the others 'shall not draw near' and the people 'shall not go up'. The speech of v 1 closes here.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('And Moses alone shall come near Yahweh: but the elders of Israel shall not come near; neither shall the people go up with him!') after Ex 19:23-24, within its reading that the creators kept people at a distance in order to be respected and safe. The canon's 'the elders of Israel' paraphrases the Hebrew *wəhēm* 'but they'. The line renders the graded access of the Hebrew and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹ֣א מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיְסַפֵּ֤ר לָעָם֙ אֵ֚ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֑ים וַיַּ֨עַן כָּל־הָעָ֜ם ק֤וֹל אֶחָד֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה נַעֲשֶֽׂה׃

i18n.en: And Moses came and told the people all the words of YHWH and all the ordinances; and all the people answered with one voice and said, "All the words which YHWH has spoken we will do."

notes.official: *kol-haddəḇārîm ʾăšer-dibber YHWH naʿăśeh* 'All the words which YHWH has spoken we will do': the first of two acclamations (cf. v 7). *hammišpāṭîm* 'the ordinances' are the laws of 21:1-23:19, which open with *wəʾēlleh hammišpāṭîm* (21:1).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּכְתֹּ֣ב מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֵ֚ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֣ם בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וַיִּ֥בֶן מִזְבֵּ֖חַ תַּ֣חַת הָהָ֑ר וּשְׁתֵּ֤ים עֶשְׂרֵה֙ מַצֵּבָ֔ה לִשְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And Moses wrote all the words of YHWH; and he rose early in the morning and built an altar at the foot of the mountain, and twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Yisra'el.

notes.official: *wayyiḵtōḇ mōšeh* 'And Moses wrote': the first explicit act of writing the covenant words, from which the 'book of the covenant' of v 7 takes its name. *ûšətêm ʿeśrēh maṣṣēḇâ* 'and twelve pillars' (central `matzevah-sacred-pillar-patriarchal-religion`), standing stones as witnesses, one for each tribe (central `shivtei-yisrael-shenim-asar-twelve-tribes-institutional-political-formula-cross-corpus`), set up with the altar 'at the foot of the mountain' (*taḥaṯ hāhār*). Deuteronomy later forbids the *maṣṣēḇâ* (Deut 16:22); this verse is one of the passages the central entry cites for its earlier acceptance in Yahwistic cult (cf. Gen 28:18; Josh 24:26-27).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח אֶֽת־נַעֲרֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּֽעֲל֖וּ עֹלֹ֑ת וַֽיִּזְבְּח֞וּ זְבָחִ֧ים שְׁלָמִ֛ים לַיהוָ֖ה פָּרִֽים׃

i18n.en: And he sent the young men of the children of Yisra'el, and they offered up burnt-offerings and sacrificed sacrifices of peace-offerings of bulls to YHWH.

notes.official: *naʿărê bənê yiśrāʾēl* 'the young men of the children of Yisra'el' perform the sacrifice, since no priesthood has yet been installed (Ex 28-29). *wayyaʿălû ʿōlōṯ wayyizbəḥû zəḇāḥîm šəlāmîm* 'and they offered up burnt-offerings and sacrificed sacrifices of peace-offerings' (central `olah-burnt-offering`; `qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`): *zəḇāḥîm šəlāmîm* is appositional, 'sacrifices, namely peace-offerings'. *pārîm* 'bulls' closes the clause in the Hebrew.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּ֤ח מֹשֶׁה֙ חֲצִ֣י הַדָּ֔ם וַיָּ֖שֶׂם בָּאַגָּנֹ֑ת וַחֲצִ֣י הַדָּ֔ם זָרַ֖ק עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

i18n.en: And Moses took half of the blood and put it in basins, and half of the blood he dashed against the altar.

notes.official: *wa-ḥăṣî haddām zāraq ʿal-hammizbēaḥ* 'and half of the blood he dashed against the altar' (ASV 'sprinkled'). The central qorbanot entry renders *zāraq* 'dash', the throwing of blood from a basin, and keeps 'sprinkle' for *hizzâ* with the finger (Milgrom, *Leviticus 1-16*, AB 3, 1991); the basins (*ʾaggānōṯ*) are named here. Half of the blood goes on the altar, on the side of YHWH, and half is kept for the people (v 8), so that the rite binds both parties (Nicholson, *God and His People*, 1986; Propp 2006).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּח֙ סֵ֣פֶר הַבְּרִ֔ית וַיִּקְרָ֖א בְּאָזְנֵ֣י הָעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה נַעֲשֶׂ֥ה וְנִשְׁמָֽע׃

i18n.en: And he took the book of the covenant and read it in the ears of the people; and they said, "All that YHWH has spoken we will do, and we will obey."

notes.official: *sēp̄er habbərîṯ* 'the book of the covenant', the written record of v 4, which gives its modern name to Ex 20:19-23:33 MT. *naʿăśeh wənišmāʿ* 'we will do, and we will obey': *šāmaʿ* covers 'hear', 'listen' and 'obey' (BDB 1, 3), and after 'we will do' the sense is obedience, as in the ASV ('be obedient'), NRSV and NJPS; exodus-woh uses 'listen' where the verb governs 'my voice' (19:5). The literal order, 'we will do and we will hear', is the basis of the rabbinic praise of Israel for committing itself to action before hearing (b. Shabbat 88a); the line keeps the sense and the literal form is given here.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּ֤ח מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶת־הַדָּ֔ם וַיִּזְרֹ֖ק עַל־הָעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֤ה דַֽם־הַבְּרִית֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר כָּרַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ עִמָּכֶ֔ם עַ֥ל כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

i18n.en: And Moses took the blood and dashed it on the people, and said, "Behold the blood of the covenant which YHWH has cut with you concerning all these words."

notes.official: *wayyizrōq ʿal-hāʿām* 'and dashed it on the people': the same verb and the same basins as v 6, so the central qorbanot rendering 'dash' also governs this use away from the altar; the two halves of the blood belong to one rite. *dam-habbərîṯ* 'the blood of the covenant' (cf. Zech 9:11; Mk 14:24 and parallels). *ʾăšer kāraṯ YHWH ʿimmāḵem* 'which YHWH has cut with you' (central `karat-brit-cut-covenant`, whose appliesTo already lists this verse in the older form EXOD-24:8).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֥עַל מֹשֶׁ֖ה וְאַהֲרֹ֑ן נָדָב֙ וַאֲבִיה֔וּא וְשִׁבְעִ֖ים מִזִּקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And Moses went up, and Aharon, Nadav and Avihu, and seventy of the elders of Yisra'el.

notes.official: The ascent of Moses, Aharon, Nadav, Avihu and the seventy elders resumes v 1. Source critics read vv 1-2, 9-11 as an account separate from the ratification of vv 3-8 (Noth, *Exodus*, OTL, 1962; Childs 1974); the line translates the text as it stands.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּרְא֕וּ אֵ֖ת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְתַ֣חַת רַגְלָ֗יו כְּמַעֲשֵׂה֙ לִבְנַ֣ת הַסַּפִּ֔יר וּכְעֶ֥צֶם הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם לָטֹֽהַר׃

i18n.en: And they saw the Elohim of Yisra'el; and under his feet there was as it were a paved work of sapphire, and as it were the very skies for clearness.

notes.official:
*wayyirʾû ʾēṯ ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl* 'And they saw the Elohim of Yisra'el' (central `elohei-yisrael`). The Hebrew states the vision with the ordinary verb *rāʾâ*, and the ancient versions soften it: the LXX has 'they saw the place where the God of Israel stood', Targum Onqelos 'they saw the glory of the God of Israel' (Propp 2006); the line translates the MT (`mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`). Nothing above the feet is described, a reticence commentators connect with 33:20 (Sarna, *Exodus*, JPS, 1991).

*wəṯaḥaṯ raḡlāyw kəmaʿăśēh liḇnaṯ hassappîr* 'and under his feet there was as it were a paved work of sapphire'. *liḇnâ* is a brick or tile, so the phrase is 'a work of tilework of *sappîr*'. The ASV adds 'stone', which is not in the Hebrew and belongs to Ezekiel's *ʾeḇen-sappîr* (Ezek 1:26; 10:1, central `eben-sapir-kisse`, whose rationale is corrected on this point in the wave diff); the line omits it (new overlay `livnat-hassappir-pavement-of-sapphire-exodus-24-10`). *sappîr* is most probably lapis lazuli, the deep-blue stone of ANE temple and throne decoration (HALOT; Sarna 1991); 'sapphire' is kept with the ASV, NRSV and NJPS. *ûḵəʿeṣem haššāmayim lāṭōhar* 'and as it were the very skies for clearness': *ʿeṣem* 'bone' yields 'the very substance' of the sky, and since the image is the colour and clarity of the physical sky, the central `shamayim` register rule gives 'skies' (ASV 'the very heaven').

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('And they saw the God of Israel: and there was under his feet as it were a paved work of a sapphire stone ...') and reads it as the description of a pedestal on which one of the creators showed himself, made of the same bluish alloy as the floor of the craft in which the message was given. The canon's English here is the KJV wording ('a paved work of a sapphire stone, and as it were the body of heaven in his clearness'), not the ASV; the French canon ('un ouvrage en plaque de saphir') has no 'pierre' and agrees with the line. The line renders *liḇnaṯ hassappîr* by its lexical sense and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וְאֶל־אֲצִילֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹ֥א שָׁלַ֖ח יָד֑וֹ וַֽיֶּחֱזוּ֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיֹּאכְל֖וּ וַיִּשְׁתּֽוּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And against the nobles of the children of Yisra'el he did not put forth his hand; and they beheld the Elohim, and they ate and drank.

notes.official: *wəʾel-ʾăṣîlê bənê yiśrāʾēl lōʾ šālaḥ yāḏô* 'And against the nobles of the children of Yisra'el he did not put forth his hand': *ʾăṣîlîm* (in this sense only here) are the leaders of v 9. The clause presupposes that seeing the deity is lethal (33:20; Gen 32:31; Judg 13:22) and records the exception. *wayyeḥĕzû ʾeṯ-hāʾĕlōhîm* 'and they beheld the Elohim': v 11 changes the verb from *rāʾâ* (v 10) to *ḥāzâ*, the verb of visionary seeing (*ḥāzôn* 'vision'), and the line keeps the contrast 'saw' / 'beheld' (ASV); the LXX again paraphrases ('they appeared in the place of God'; `mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`). *wayyōʾḵəlû wayyištû* 'and they ate and drank': the covenant meal in the presence of the deity (cf. Gen 26:30; 31:54; Nicholson 1986).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה עֲלֵ֥ה אֵלַ֛י הָהָ֖רָה וֶהְיֵה־שָׁ֑ם וְאֶתְּנָ֨ה לְךָ֜ אֶת־לֻחֹ֣ת הָאֶ֗בֶן וְהַתּוֹרָה֙ וְהַמִּצְוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּתַ֖בְתִּי לְהוֹרֹתָֽם׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said to Moses, "Come up to me on the mountain and be there, and I will give you the tablets of stone, and the law and the commandment which I have written, to teach them."

notes.official: *wəʾettənâ ləḵā ʾeṯ-luḥōṯ hāʾeḇen wəhattôrâ wəhammiṣwâ ʾăšer kāṯaḇtî ləhôrōṯām* 'and I will give you the tablets of stone, and the law and the commandment which I have written, to teach them'. *tôrâ* is rendered 'law' where it names a written body of law (new central `torah-law-instruction-rendering-cross-corpus`, which also governs Deut 4:8, 44 and the Kings sites); exodus-woh's 'torah' at 13:9 and 16:4, where the word has the broader sense 'instruction', stands, and unifying the two renderings is a founder point. The syntax is disputed: the *wə* before *hattôrâ* can be explicative, 'the tablets of stone, that is, the law and the commandment' (Rashi; many moderns), or simply coordinating (ASV); the line keeps the ambiguity of the Hebrew. *ləhôrōṯām* 'to teach them' is from *yrh*, the root of *tôrâ*.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֣קָם מֹשֶׁ֔ה וִיהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ מְשָׁרְת֑וֹ וַיַּ֥עַל מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל־הַ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

i18n.en: And Moses rose, and Yehoshua his attendant; and Moses went up to the mountain of the Elohim.

notes.official: *wîhôšuaʿ məšārəṯô* 'and Yehoshua his attendant' (ASV 'minister'; Yehoshua = Joshua): *məšārēṯ* is a personal attendant (33:11; Num 11:28; 1 Kgs 19:21 of Elisha). *har hāʾĕlōhîm* 'the mountain of the Elohim' (central `har-sinai-horev-the-mountain-of-Elohim-divine-mountain-cross-corpus`, as 3:1).

paragraphs.text: וְאֶל־הַזְּקֵנִ֤ים אָמַר֙ שְׁבוּ־לָ֣נוּ בָזֶ֔ה עַ֥ד אֲשֶׁר־נָשׁ֖וּב אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וְהִנֵּ֨ה אַהֲרֹ֤ן וְחוּר֙ עִמָּכֶ֔ם מִי־בַ֥עַל דְּבָרִ֖ים יִגַּ֥שׁ אֲלֵהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And to the elders he said, "Wait here for us until we return to you; and behold, Aharon and Chur are with you: whoever has a matter, let him go near to them."

notes.official: *šəḇû-lānû ḇāzeh* 'Wait here for us'. *mî-ḇaʿal dəḇārîm* 'whoever has a matter', literally 'a master of words', i.e. a party with a case to be judged (cf. 18:16, 22). Chur (ASV Hur) is named with Aharon as at 17:10-12.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֥עַל מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל־הָהָ֑ר וַיְכַ֥ס הֶעָנָ֖ן אֶת־הָהָֽר׃

i18n.en: And Moses went up to the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.

notes.official: *wayḵas heʿānān ʾeṯ-hāhār* 'and the cloud covered the mountain'. The cloud has the article: the known cloud of the divine presence (13:21-22; 19:9, 16), and the register of the central `sinai-theophany-ex-19-elohim-craft-descent-disavowals-volcanic-hypothesis-cross-corpus` is extended to vv 15-18. Verses 15b-18a are usually assigned to the Priestly source, which speaks of *kāḇôḏ* and *šāḵan* (Childs 1974; Propp 2006).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁכֹּ֤ן כְּבוֹד־יְהוָה֙ עַל־הַ֣ר סִינַ֔י וַיְכַסֵּ֥הוּ הֶעָנָ֖ן שֵׁ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֑ים וַיִּקְרָ֧א אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֛ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י מִתּ֥וֹךְ הֶעָנָֽן׃

i18n.en: And the glory of YHWH dwelt upon Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days; and on the seventh day he called to Moses from the midst of the cloud.

notes.official: *wayyiškōn kəḇôḏ-YHWH ʿal-har sînay* 'And the glory of YHWH dwelt upon Mount Sinai' (ASV 'abode'). *šāḵan* 'dwell, settle' takes 'dwell' under the central `shakhan-dwell-divine-presence-verb-cross-corpus`; it is the root of *miškān* 'tabernacle' (25:8-9), and its use here anticipates the move of the glory from the mountain to the sanctuary (40:34-35). *kəḇôḏ-YHWH* 'the glory of YHWH' (central `kavod-yhwh`). The six days and the call 'on the seventh day' have been compared with the seven days of Gen 1:1-2:3 (Sarna 1991; Propp 2006).

paragraphs.text: וּמַרְאֵה֙ כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֔ה כְּאֵ֥שׁ אֹכֶ֖לֶת בְּרֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֑ר לְעֵינֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And the appearance of the glory of YHWH was like a devouring fire on the top of the mountain before the eyes of the children of Yisra'el.

notes.official:
*ûmarʾēh kəḇôḏ YHWH kəʾēš ʾōḵeleṯ bərōʾš hāhār* 'And the appearance of the glory of YHWH was like a devouring fire on the top of the mountain'. *kəʾēš ʾōḵeleṯ* is a simile, 'like a fire that consumes'; without the comparative particle the same phrase is a predicate of YHWH at Deut 4:24 and 9:3 ('a devouring fire'). The line keeps the ASV 'devouring', with the English indefinite article for the count noun (NJPS 'a consuming fire'). The verse gives the view of the people below (*ləʿênê bənê yiśrāʾēl*), as v 10 gave that of the elders (central `kavod-yhwh`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('the sight of the glory of Yahweh was like devouring fire on the top of the mount') and reads the 'glory' as the creators' flying craft, which takes on a fire-like colour at the moment of departure. The line renders *kāḇôḏ* 'glory' under the central entry and the simile literally; neither encodes a craft.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א מֹשֶׁ֛ה בְּת֥וֹךְ הֶעָנָ֖ן וַיַּ֣עַל אֶל־הָהָ֑ר וַיְהִ֤י מֹשֶׁה֙ בָּהָ֔ר אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים לָֽיְלָה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And Moses entered into the midst of the cloud and went up to the mountain; and Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.

notes.official: Moses enters 'the midst of the cloud' (*bəṯôḵ heʿānān*), from which YHWH called him (v 16). The forty days and forty nights recur at 34:28 and Deut 9:9, 18 (cf. 1 Kgs 19:8, Eliyahu at Horeb). The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) closes the narrative; Ex 25-31 is a single divine speech.
